# Temple Scroll Column 45 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 45 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 45:1 — "vulture/osprey" vs. "bearded vulture/black vulture" vs. "vulture/osprey" — raptor identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the vulture, and the osprey" | Traditional renderings |
| LOGOS | "the bearded vulture, and the black vulture" | Precise ornithological terms |
| PNEUMA | "the vulture, and the osprey" | Same as EMET |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/PNEUMA renderings. The precise species are uncertain; traditional terms are more recognizable.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/PNEUMA.

---

## 45:5 — "cormorant/great owl" vs. "fisher owl/long-eared owl" vs. "fishing owl/screech owl" — owl identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the cormorant and the great owl" | Traditional renderings |
| LOGOS | "the fisher owl and the long-eared owl" | Ornithological precision |
| PNEUMA | "the fishing owl and the screech owl" | Modern equivalents |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "the cormorant and the great owl." Traditional renderings favored when identification is uncertain.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 45:7 — "desert owl/carrion vulture" vs. "desert owl/Egyptian vulture" vs. "pelican/carrion vulture" — bird identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the desert owl and the carrion vulture" | Traditional |
| LOGOS | "the desert owl and the Egyptian vulture" | Ornithological |
| PNEUMA | "the pelican and the carrion vulture" | Alternative identification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Compromise: adopted "the carrion vulture and the Egyptian vulture" drawing from both EMET and LOGOS to distinguish the two species listed.

**Status:** Resolved as compromise.

---

## 45:11 — "break his word" vs. "violate his word" vs. "go back on his word" — vow-breaking verb

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he shall not break his word" | Literal yachel |
| LOGOS | "he shall not violate his word" | Formal legal term |
| PNEUMA | "he must not go back on his word" | Colloquial expression |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "break his word" per EMET. Simple and accurate for yachel.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 45:13 — "sin in you" vs. "guilt shall be upon you" vs. "you will bear guilt" — chet consequence

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "there shall be sin in you" | Literal chet rendering |
| LOGOS | "guilt shall be upon you" | Interprets chet as guilt |
| PNEUMA | "you will bear guilt" | Dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "there shall be sin in you" per EMET. "Sin" for chet is the project standard.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 45:16 — "profane his word" vs. "profane his word" vs. "treat his spoken word lightly" — chalal rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he shall not profane his word" | Literal chalal |
| LOGOS | "he shall not profane his word" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "no one may treat his spoken word lightly" | Dynamic interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "profane his word" per EMET and LOGOS. Chalal means to desecrate or profane, which is stronger than merely treating lightly.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
